name: @cloudsforge/beacon
description: The release gate. Synthetic probes and user journeys on a leased schedule, incidents with hysteresis and dedupe, SLOs whose error budget is integer arithmetic, conformance runs, Prometheus metrics, and a redacted public status projection that cannot leak a field it was not told about. A release promotes only if this service says so, and an unknown is never a pass.

scripts._smoke: The estate in a real browser, stubbing nothing. Separate from `test` on purpose: `test` SKIPS the browser half where no estate answers, which is right for a test run and fatal for a pipeline, so a deploy script runs THIS and gets exit 2 rather than a green when nothing was there to look at.
scripts._test: --test-concurrency=1 is required, not a preference: every database test file truncates this service's tables between cases, and node:test runs FILES in parallel by default. A TRUNCATE takes an AccessExclusiveLock, so one file's reset deadlocks against another file's inserts (40P01). Cases within a file already run in order.
scripts._testGlob: src/browser/*.test.ts is named EXPLICITLY. A shell glob does not recurse, so adding a directory under src/ and nothing else would have left its tests unrun while the suite went green — which is the same defect as a CI job that builds an image and never boots it.

_localDependencies: Every sibling takes 'link:', not 'file:'. A 'file:' path PACKS the dependency, and each of
these packages declares files: ['dist'] with a publishConfig that points main/types at dist/.
Packing therefore installs a package whose exports resolve to a dist/ that has not been built,
while its 'main' in the working tree still says src/index.ts. 'link:' symlinks the checkout in
place, so the working-tree manifest is the one that is read and the package keeps using its own
tsx is a runtime dependency because the unpublished packages resolve to their TypeScript
sources. On publish their publishConfig points at dist/, tsx moves to devDependencies, and the
hearth-wallet-core is the odd one out: it is not a runtime package and not a contract, it is
the SIGNER, and beacon takes it for exactly one journey. BJ-DEX-02 has to sign a swap in a
browser that has no wallet extension, and 25-wallet-clients.md section 3 names divergent copies
of a signer as the worst failure that design can have. Writing secp256k1 and legacy RLP here to
save a dependency would be the fourth divergence. It has no dependencies of its own, so unlike
runtime and contracts it needs no install step of its own in the image.
_optionalDependencies: playwright-core, NOT playwright. The full package downloads its own browser build at install
time and takes the image from roughly 200MB to 1.5GB; playwright-core is the same driver API
against a Chromium the image already has. The frozen repository recorded this reason at
stack/infra/beacon/src/browser.js:9-11 and it has not changed.
OPTIONAL, so that a deployment choosing not to ship a browser installs nothing extra and every
browser journey skips with that reason rather than failing. src/browser/driver.ts declares the
slice of the API it uses structurally rather than importing its types, so `tsc` does not need
the package to be present either — an optional runtime dependency that is a mandatory build
